title: Smudge
logline: A tiny ink smudge nobody wanted in the comic becomes the only thing holding the story together.
look: Bold cel shading, clean ink lines, primary colours; comic-page gutters as white void; smears, speed lines, impact frames, long holds.
narrator: female, young adult, moderate pitch, american accent
Bright, playful comic-book narrator with comic timing
music: Brassy cartoon hero theme with snare; pizzicato for Smudge; a full-orchestra hit on the rescue; ends on a cheeky woodblock.

shots.direction: CU 50mm · locked · cut — a blank comic page; a pen nib slams down (impact frame)
WS 35mm · locked · cut — inside a panel, Captain Bright poses heroically; in the white gutter, a tiny ink smudge with eyes: Smudge
MS 50mm · locked · cut — Smudge copies the hero's pose; an eraser swipes him off the panel edge (smear); he pops back
MS 35mm · whip pans · cut — the hero fights a cartoon villain; Smudge jumps in to help and is kicked out of frame
CU 85mm · long hold · cut — Smudge sits alone in the white gutter
WS 24mm · whip pan · smash cut — the villain's giant hook rips the page; a tear opens across the panels; the hero falls
CU 50mm · shake · cut — the hero dangles over the tear, slipping (impact frame)
MS 35mm · push in · cut — Smudge looks at the tear and stretches himself across it, a living stitch (squash and stretch)
WS 24mm · speed lines · cut — the hero runs across Smudge to safety and lands the final punch (impact frames)
CU 85mm · hold · cut — Smudge, thin as a line, exhausted, still holding the page together
MS 50mm · slow push · cut — the hero kneels and offers a hand; the panel border redraws around both of them
WS 35mm · locked · cut — the last panel: hero and Smudge posing together, Smudge tiny and proud
WS · page-turn wipe · cut to black — a fresh blank page; Smudge peeks in from the corner

narration.text: Every page has a hero. This is not him.
Smudge was the mistake nobody erased in time.
But mistakes are very good at filling gaps.
Heroes save the story. Somebody has to hold it together.
Turn the page. He's still there.
